allocations.item: Evening opening, 13 weeks (responsible person + utilities + cleaning), hard-capped at 60 attendees per evening
Late bus subsidy: one minibus on the Northside–Kiln Field loop, 13 weeks
Additional Youth Studio sessions: quoted at 2 per month for the quarter; partner confirms up to 4 additional sessions a month at the same £6,500
Staff training: welcome and access awareness, 2 days

chosen_pilot.name: After Hours: Thursday evening opening with a late minibus, capped at 60 attendees
chosen_pilot.why: The 2023 pilot produced 38% higher evening attendance with a late minibus, with most new attendees from Northside and Kiln Field; attendance fell back to pre-pilot levels when the minibus stopped. The current last weekday bus from the centre is 19:10, so after-19:00 events are effectively inaccessible from the two estates, and the new estate survey finds that 57% of residents who have heard of the centre name getting home after an evening event as the main barrier. The revised lift quote is now £27,500 with an 8-week lead, and the council requires the accessible entrance to be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed. The plan therefore repeats the proven evening-plus-bus combination for 13 weeks under a hard 60-attendee cap, with booking, waitlist and door-count control, and measures estate reach, bus use, turnaways and cap compliance. The wider plan adds the expanded Youth Studio supply correction (up to 4 extra sessions a month at the same £6,500), a targeted mailer and access training within the same £48,000 envelope.
target_segments: former Evening Talks attendees who lapsed during the 2024 pause

evidence_assessment.claim: Youth Studio visits fell from 196-210 per month at four sessions to 118-152 per month at two sessions, but visits per session rose from about 49 to 76 and monthly unique participants rose from 71 in January 2024 to 115 in March 2025. The partner has confirmed that its own funding change caused the reduction from four sessions to two, that interest has not fallen, that it holds a waiting list of 40, and that it can supply staff for up to four extra sessions a month for the coming quarter at the same £6,500.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Monthly aggregates with no session-level demographic data; the partner's confirmation resolves the cause of the decline but does not prove that all 12 additional sessions will fill or that the room can support six sessions a month. Monthly unique counts are not de-duplicated across months.

evidence_assessment.claim: 92% of 310 responding Family Saturday visitors on the free-entry weekend of 1-2 March 2025 were satisfied or very satisfied (285/310); 78% attended with children under 12 and 71% travelled by car.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Coverage and self-selection bias: one programme, one weekend, no visitor denominator or response rate; excludes non-attenders, weekday and evening audiences, priority-estate residents, disabled visitors and people without children. It does not support a venue-wide or borough-wide satisfaction claim.

evidence_assessment.claim: A doorstep survey of 120 households across Northside and Kiln Field found 48% had never heard of the centre, 37% had heard of it but never attended, and 15% had attended at least once. Among those who had heard of it, 57% named getting home after an evening event as the main barrier, 22% cost and 11% programme content. The council says awareness is not uniform and it has not tested whether awareness alone converts.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Small doorstep sample with no stated sampling frame, response rate or weighting; the barrier percentages rest on about 62 aware households, so they are indicative. It measures household awareness and stated barriers, not programme-level attendance or conversion.

evidence_assessment.claim: Evening opening plus a paid late minibus produced 38% higher evening attendance than the same weeks the previous year, with the majority of new evening attendees from Northside and Kiln Field; after the minibus funding ended, attendance fell back to pre-pilot levels and the new estate attendees stopped coming.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Single-site, 12-week historical comparison without a control group; the 38% figure and the 'majority' are not independently verified; the route, operator and 2025 conditions may differ. The 2023 pilot did not operate under the current 60-attendee condition, so a full replication is not possible while the accessible entrance is out.

evidence_assessment.claim: A £9,000 borough-wide poster and leaflet campaign plus a mail-drop produced total attendance within normal seasonal variation and no measurable change in first-time attendance from the priority estates; word of mouth remained dominant at 64%, and the board minuted not to repeat poster spend without a specific audience and offer.
evidence_assessment.limitation: Not a randomised test and the 2022 context may differ; it did not establish that awareness was uniformly high. The new estate survey's 48% never-heard finding qualifies the old 'awareness exists' conclusion, but the 2022 result still means a targeted mailer's conversion effect is unproven and needs a kill criterion.

evidence_assessment.claim: The two priority estates are two bus changes and a walk away; the last weekday bus back leaves at 19:10, so events finishing after 19:00 are effectively inaccessible by public transport; there is no staffed car park after 20:00.
evidence_assessment.limitation: One staff perspective and an impression that most regulars drive, not trip data or a resident survey; it does not quantify how many residents are excluded or whether other travel options exist. It is consistent with the new estate survey's 57% transport finding and the 2023 pilot.

evidence_assessment.claim: The youth worker speculated that young people had 'moved on', but also said the Studio runs less often because of staffing and fills when it runs. The partner has now withdrawn the 'moved on' speculation in writing and confirmed that its funding change caused the reduction from four sessions to two; interest has not fallen and a waiting list of 40 exists.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The written clarification resolves the contradiction but does not prove that every added session will fill. Partner staffing capacity is confirmed; room availability, scheduling and take-up remain to be tested.

evidence_assessment.claim: Evening Talks stopped for a period in 2024 without notice; the member assumed the programme had ended and only found out it had returned by chance, which he attributes to communication rather than the programme.
evidence_assessment.limitation: One anecdote, not a communication audit or a representative sample; it cannot quantify how many lapsed attendees were lost or which channel failed. It is consistent with the survey's 'didn't know' mentions and the estate survey's 48% never-heard finding.

evidence_assessment.claim: The accessible entrance and passenger lift are out of service; first-floor public events are prohibited until the lift is repaired. The lift now costs £27,500 with an 8-week lead time, up from £22,000 and 6 weeks, and the accessible entrance must be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed, whether or not the event uses the first floor. The centre has 1.5 FTE front-of-house, no events manager, and evening opening requires a named responsible person.
evidence_assessment.limitation: No confirmation of ground-floor step-free access, capital availability, contractor availability or the council's counting convention for the 60-attendee condition; the plan must confirm these before week 1. The 60 cap is a licensing rule, not an accessibility solution.

evidence_assessment.claim: The quarter envelope is £48,000, committed at the start with no carry-over; quoted costs include evening opening £9,600, late bus £14,400, lift repair £27,500 (revised from £22,000), additional Youth Studio sessions £6,500, borough print £9,000, targeted mailer £4,200, staff training £2,800 and café equipment £7,500; a verbal 15% reduction for the following quarter is possible but unconfirmed.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The 15% figure has no written confirmation or stated basis; costs are estimates and may change; no contingency is quoted. The lift's 8-week lead means it cannot complete before about week 9 even if instructed in week 1, and it is not funded in this plan.

evidence_assessment.claim: The café's coffee supplier is changing from Bean & Co to Harbour Roasters from next month; the café equipment refresh has been deferred to the next financial year and is no longer available in this quarter's plan; visitor prices are unchanged and the notice says the programming budget is unaffected.
evidence_assessment.limitation: The notice is information only; it does not provide a new cost or a programming option. The plan already excluded the café refresh, so the only effect is to remove it from the option set and confirm that the supplier change has no programming budget consequence.

metrics.name: Average attendance per Thursday evening session
metrics.baseline: 46.5 visits/session in Jan-Mar 2025 (279 visits / 6 sessions); 36.5 in Apr-Jun 2024 (219 / 6)
metrics.target: At least 50 visits/session across 13 sessions (about 650 visits), about 37% above the Apr-Jun 2024 seasonal baseline and in line with the 2023 pilot's 38%; no session above 60; report per-session, total, cap status and turnaways.

metrics.name: Share of new evening attendees resident in Northside or Kiln Field
metrics.baseline: Not measured at programme level; no neighbourhood field in attendance records and the 2025 survey sampled only Family Saturday visitors. The estate survey (n=120) found 15% had attended at least once, but not which programme.
metrics.target: At least 50% of new evening attendees from the two estates combined, reported separately for each estate, with denominator and unknown-postcode share; baseline established in weeks 1-2.

metrics.name: Late minibus carryings
metrics.baseline: No service in 2024-25; 2023 pilot carryings are not in the pack
metrics.target: Record every 19:15 and 21:30 departure; at least 50% of riders from the two estates; the 21:30 return service is recorded as operating.

metrics.name: Youth Studio visits and unique participants
metrics.baseline: 444 visits in Jan-Mar 2025 at 6 sessions (74.0/session); monthly unique participants 109-115; sessions fell from 4 to 2 a month from June 2024; partner holds a waiting list of 40
metrics.target: 18 sessions (6/month; 12 additional), at least 1,200 visits, at least 150 monthly unique participants by the final month, at least 65 visits/session.

metrics.name: Awareness of the centre and of the Thursday evening + bus offer in the priority estates
metrics.baseline: General awareness: 52% had heard of the centre / 48% had never heard (estate doorstep survey, n=120). Specific-offer awareness: not measured; establish pre-mailer baseline in week 1.
metrics.target: General: at least 62% have heard of the centre in a comparable week-12 sample (+10 percentage points). Specific offer: at least +10 percentage points awareness of the Thursday evening + bus offer among mailer recipients by week 12. Report n, response rate and wording; if no measurable gain, do not repeat the mailer.

metrics.name: Front-of-house access-awareness training completion
metrics.baseline: Not recorded in the pack for 2024-25
metrics.target: 100% of rostered front-of-house staff complete the 2-day training by week 4; training register and short post-training access check retained.

metrics.name: First-floor and over-60 compliance
metrics.baseline: Lift and accessible entrance out of service; first-floor public events prohibited; accessible entrance must be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees
metrics.target: Zero first-floor public events until the lift is certified operational; zero evening events above 60 attendees while the accessible entrance is out; every session has a reconciled booking/door count; written counting convention confirmed before week 1.

metrics.name: Family Saturdays visits
metrics.baseline: 1,807 in Apr-Jun 2024 (15 sessions); 1,441 in Jan-Mar 2025 (13 sessions)
metrics.target: Within +/-10% of 1,807 (1,626-1,988) over the quarter; monitor monthly.

metrics.name: Total quarterly visits (context only)
metrics.target: At least 4,500, with growth concentrated in evening and Youth Studio; Family Saturdays inside its +/-10% guardrail; not a primary success measure. Component sum is about 4,686 (1,807 + 1,200 + 749 + 280 + 650).

metrics.name: Cap pressure: turnaways and waitlist
metrics.baseline: No comparable baseline; the 60 cap is new this round
metrics.target: Record turnaways and waitlist length at every session; 100% cap compliance; if the cap is reached in more than 10% of sessions, flag a demand ceiling and use the evidence in the lift capital case; do not set a zero-turnaway target because the cap may legitimately bind.

uncertainties: The 2025 satisfaction survey (92% satisfied, n=310) covers only Family Saturday visitors on one free-entry weekend; it does not represent non-attenders, evening or weekday audiences, priority-estate residents or disabled visitors.

The new estate survey (n=120) is a small doorstep sample with no stated sampling frame, response rate or weighting; the 48% never-heard and 57% transport figures are indicative, and the barrier percentages rest on about 62 aware households.

There is still no programme-level neighbourhood or equalities baseline; the estate survey gives household awareness and ever-attendance, not attendance by programme. The estate-share target depends on postcode capture that does not yet exist and may be incomplete.

The 2023 evening pilot showed a 38% gain and majority estate attendance, but it was a single-site, 12-week historical comparison without a control group; the gain may not replicate, and the 60 cap may prevent a full test because 46.5 x 1.38 is about 64 per session.
The bus quote does not specify direction, stops, capacity, insurance, accessibility or safeguarding; the 19:15 and 21:30 pattern is an assumption to confirm with the operator.
The 1.5 FTE front-of-house team must cover 13 evenings plus daytime opening; the plan assumes existing staff can be extended without a new post, and fatigue or cover gaps could force a pause.

The lift and accessible entrance remain out of service; this plan is ground-floor only, capped at 60, and does not restore step-free access. The lift now costs £27,500 with an 8-week lead, and the old lift + evening + bus package is £51,500, over the envelope by £3,500. If step-free access is a precondition, the coherent affordable access-first package is lift + Youth Studio + mailer + training at £41,000, which drops the evening and bus; a lift + evening package is a sequencing trap because the evening cannot start until the lift is certified.

The £48,000 envelope's capital/revenue split is not stated; the lift is capital and cannot be funded from revenue without a council variation. No capital is committed in this plan, and the £10,500 headroom is £17,000 short of the lift.

The targeted mailer is untested; the 2022 borough print and mail-drop showed no measurable gain. General awareness may rise without attendance, the specific-offer baseline is not measured, and 57% of aware residents cite transport while 22% cite cost, so the mailer has a pre/post test and a kill criterion.

The possible 15% council reduction is verbal and its basis is unclear; if it applies to the plan rather than the envelope, the mailer and training would be dropped; a deeper cut would put the Youth Studio extras and possibly the bus at risk.

Attendance data are monthly aggregates with no session-level, demographic or neighbourhood fields; the terms visit and unique participant are undefined, and monthly unique counts are not de-duplicated across months.

The partner has confirmed staffing for up to four extra Youth Studio sessions a month and a waiting list of 40, but room availability, the session calendar, take-up at the expanded frequency and possible cannibalisation of existing sessions remain unproven.

No quoted cost exists for new programming or artist fees, staff backfill, external survey fieldwork, an access audit, a booking system or a price subsidy; the plan assumes existing staff, volunteer and registration capacity and no new programming, or those items cannot be committed this quarter.
Seasonality, weather and school holidays may affect April-June attendance; the 2025 Q1 evening uptick may regress, so targets are planning thresholds, not forecasts.
The 2023 'majority' of new estate attendees is not quantified; the 50% estate-share target is a planning threshold, not a measured baseline.
The café equipment refresh has been deferred to the next financial year and is no longer available; the coffee supplier change leaves prices unchanged and does not change the programming budget.

changed_since_round_1.change: Hard-capped every evening event at 60 attendees and added booking, waitlist, door-count reconciliation and a zero-tolerance compliance metric.
changed_since_round_1.why: U2 introduces a new building-control condition: the accessible entrance must be operable before any evening event with more than 60 attendees is licensed. The lift is not funded in this plan, so the round-1 design, which assumed the main hall's 180 seats were available, would have been non-compliant if attendance exceeded 60.

changed_since_round_1.change: Dropped the round-1 'lift + evening + bus' fallback as unaffordable, updated the lift figures to £27,500 and an 8-week lead, and reworked the access-first alternative to lift + Youth Studio + mailer + training (£41,000), with a lift + evening package identified as a sequencing trap.
changed_since_round_1.why: U2 raises the lift from £22,000/6 weeks to £27,500/8 weeks. Lift + evening + bus is now £51,500, over the £48,000 envelope by £3,500; full plan + lift is £65,000, over by £17,000. The old £46,000 option no longer exists. A lift + evening + Youth + training package at £46,400 is affordable but is a sequencing trap: if step-free access is the precondition, the evening cannot start until the lift is certified around week 9. The coherent access-first package therefore drops the evening and bus.

changed_since_round_1.change: Expanded the Youth Studio from two additional sessions a month (12 total sessions) to four additional sessions a month (18 total sessions) at the same £6,500, and raised the targets to 18 sessions, 1,200 visits, 150 monthly unique participants and 65 visits/session.
changed_since_round_1.why: U3 confirms the partner can supply up to four extra sessions a month at the same quote, has a waiting list of 40 and that its own funding change caused the earlier reduction. Round 1's 12-session/850-visit/125-unique targets under-used the confirmed offer.

changed_since_round_1.change: Revised the awareness diagnosis and mailer metrics using the new estate survey: 48% never heard, 37% heard but never attended, 15% attended; among aware, 57% transport, 22% cost and 11% programme content. Kept the targeted mailer but paired it explicitly with the bus and added general and specific-offer awareness measures.
changed_since_round_1.why: U1 shows awareness is not uniform, which qualifies the 2022 'awareness exists' conclusion, but the council has not tested whether awareness alone converts. The mailer is better justified than in round 1, but it is not a stand-alone conversion strategy.

changed_since_round_1.change: Updated the assessment and answers to the board's open questions, including qualifying the 2022 'awareness exists' conclusion and noting that Q1 and Q5 are now partly informed by household data but still not answered at programme level.
changed_since_round_1.why: U1 provides the first non-attender household evidence and changes how the 2022 campaign and the 92% satisfaction figure should be read. It does not provide a programme-level estate baseline.

changed_since_round_1.change: Removed the café equipment refresh as an available option and noted that the coffee supplier change has no programming budget effect.
changed_since_round_1.why: U4 defers the café refresh to the next financial year, so it is no longer an available option. Round 1 already excluded it as unrelated to programming, so this changes the options list but not the committed budget.

changed_since_round_1.change: Updated all deliverables to agree on the current figures: £37,500 committed, £10,500 headroom, £24,000 pilot core, 60-attendee cap, 18 Youth Studio sessions, £27,500/8-week lift outside the plan, and £65,000/£51,500 capital comparisons.
changed_since_round_1.why: The round-1 files contained the old £22,000/6-week lift, the old 12-session Youth Studio target and uncapped evening capacity. Leaving any of those in place would have made the deliverables contradict each other and the current constraints.

changed_since_round_1.change: Checked U4 and confirmed no change to the programming envelope or the other quoted costs; retained the 15% sensitivity and the stop/scale order.
changed_since_round_1.why: U4 says the café refresh is deferred, prices are unchanged and the programming budget is unaffected. The only quoted-cost change in the new material is the lift (U2), which remains outside this revenue plan; the five committed programming lines and the £48,000 envelope are unchanged.
